client_situation.text: The RFP is issued by the City of Federal Way, Washington, which incorporated in February 1990 and changed from a council-manager to a mayor-council form of government in November 2010.

The City is a residential and commercial municipality with an estimated 22,485 people employed within its city limits, and its comprehensive plan targets a vibrant City Center with mixed-use development and public transit access.

The City's current ERP environment is described only in tables in Section 3 Scope that are not reproduced in the RFP text, so bidders must obtain the current-systems table to know what is being replaced.
The City's stated driver is process improvement through new systems, with adoption of the best practices offered by the selected Vendor.
The City wants a Vendor with experience successfully implementing the proposed solutions for cities of similar size and scope of services.
The City is open to best-of-breed Human Capital Management responses from Vendors that are not ERP providers, provided the HCM solution can integrate with the selected ERP system.

goal.text: The City intends to purchase an integrated ERP solution covering the modules and functionality defined in the separate Requirements document issued with the RFP.
The City expects the replacement ERP to be implemented in a phased approach, or as recommended by the selected Vendor and approved by the City.

Required Financial modules are General Ledger, Budget, Project and Grant Accounting, Purchasing and Contract Management, Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, Capital Assets and Enterprise Cashiering, sized at 130 named users and 85 concurrent users.
Required Human Capital Management modules are Human Resources, Time and Attendance and Payroll, sized at 400 FTEs and 744 W2s.
Implementation is scheduled for March 2025 through January 2027, with Go Live for all modules in scope required by January 1, 2027.

The Vendor must deliver implementation services covering software deployment, data conversion, system configuration, report development, testing and training, plus a sample project plan, process improvement strategy, business change management methodology, data conversion methodology by module, and testing and training methodologies.

The Vendor must provide post go-live tools and services, backup and disaster recovery services, and support with stated hours, guaranteed response time, escalation process and baseline versus premium levels.

success_criteria.text: Proposals are scored on five weighted criteria: Software 30 points, Implementation 25 points, Technology 15 points, Vendor 15 points and Cost Value 15 points.
The Implementation criterion explicitly requires Go Live for all modules in scope by January 1, 2027.

Finalists must present functional and technical product demos to the City following a pre-defined Demo Script supplied in the invitation, and demo evaluation covers adherence to that script and demonstrated ability to meet the City's functional and technical requirements.

Every Requirements line item must be rated and commented, with ratings of 4 (standard/configuration), 3 (third-party integrated, named), 2 (modification, with estimated cost), 0 (not available) or F (future release, with month and year), and blank responses may cause rejection as incomplete.
Software missing a significant number of required features and technology preferences may be eliminated from consideration.
Vendor questions are due August 28, 2024 at 3:00 p.m. PT, answers are posted September 5, 2024, and proposals are due September 17, 2024 at 3:00 p.m. PT, with late submissions not considered.

The selection schedule runs finalists in October 2024, software demos in December 2024, due diligence in January 2025, and contract negotiations from January 2025 onward, and the City reserves the right to modify or reschedule it.
No contract will be awarded until it is approved by City Council.

constraints.text: Proposals must be emailed to Thuch.Mam@FederalWayWA.gov as one electronic PDF of no more than 100 pages (sample contract excluded) plus one completed Requirements document in MS Word format, and fax submittals are not acceptable.

The Requirements document is a separate Word file that becomes Section 2 of the proposal; its format, font, numbering and page breaks must not be changed, each response is limited to 100 words, and hyperlinks or cross-references to other line items are prohibited.

Pricing must use the Exhibit A template, be comprehensive including all taxes and available discounts, remain valid for 180 days from the response date, and include license/maintenance cost for Years 1 through 10 with a separate sheet per deployment option (SaaS or on-premises).
Vendors must supply three current and two prior customer references on Exhibit B forms, similar in size and scope to the City's project, with preference for Washington State public sector clients.
Vendors must disclose any contract terminated for convenience, non-performance or other reason in the past five years, or any legal action with a customer, naming the contracting party and address.

The technology overview must cover hosted, on-premises and SaaS architecture options, data center locations and redundancy, hardware specifications, mobile hardware and OS options, remote access, integration tools and methodologies, and update scheduling.

The security overview must address the security model and standards, security administration including SSO and SAML, multi-factor authentication, and security breach customer communication, response and cost.
All data, materials and documentation originated and prepared for the City under the solicitation belong to the City, and no Vendor may mark its entire submittal proprietary.

chunk_summaries.summary: The RFP is issued by the City of Federal Way for Enterprise Resource Planning Software and Implementation Services. Issue date: August 16, 2024. Contact and RFP questions to Thuch Mam at Thuch.Mam@FederalWayWA.gov. Questions are due August 28, 2024 at 3:00 p.m. PT. Proposals are due September 17, 2024 at 3:00 p.m. PT. Vendor responses must be received by the City of Federal Way no later than the indicated date, time and location; late submissions will not be considered and fax submittals are not acceptable.

The City of Federal Way (City) seeks proposals from experienced and qualified Vendors to provide ERP software and services satisfying all of the City's functional and technical requirements. The preferred Vendor shall have experience successfully implementing the proposed solutions for cities of similar size and scope of services; detailed product and service requirements are in Section 3 - Scope of Work and Timeline of this RFP. The City is also open to responses from Vendors providing best of breed solutions for Human Capital Management, which must have the ability to integrate with the selected ERP system; such Vendors complete the Requirements template in Section 6 for the relevant functionality and submit per instructions in Section 5. The submitter is responsible for delivering proposals by the date and time indicated in the RFP; the City accepts no responsibility for lost or misdirected email submittals, is not liable for costs incurred before contract issuance, and all proposal costs are the Vendor's responsibility. All materials submitted become the City's property, are public documents, will not be returned, and submission constitutes acknowledgment and acceptance of all terms and conditions in the RFP and its exhibits and attachments.

The City began in the late 1800s as a logging settlement; Federal Highway 99 was complete by the 1920s, linking the community to Seattle and Tacoma. The name Federal Way was first used in 1929 when five existing schools consolidated into School District #210 and planned Federal Way High School next to Highway 99. By the end of the 1950s the community had housing areas and a 10-block commercial district with a shopping center and family-oriented theme park; the 1960s brought residential development for Boeing engineers and Weyerhaeuser executives, and SeaTac Mall was built in the mid-1970s. The City incorporated in February 1990 as then Washington's sixth largest city, and in November 2010 citizens changed from a council-manager to a mayor-council form of government. Today the City is residential and commercial, with an estimated 22,485 people employed within the city limits, and its comprehensive plan includes a vibrant City Center with mixed-use development and access to public transportation.

The City intends to purchase an integrated ERP solution that includes the modules and functionality defined in the Requirements document provided with this RFP. The City expects to implement a replacement ERP solution using a phased approach, or as recommended by the selected Vendor and approved by the City. The City expects process improvement through implementation of new systems and intends to adopt the best practices offered by the selected Vendor. Vendors invited to demonstrate their product should be prepared to discuss the application's best practices and the system's ability to adapt to user preferences.

The chunk introduces tables that outline the current environment at the City and designate which solutions are considered part of the scope for this project. No specific systems, dates, amounts or constraints are given in this chunk; the tables themselves are not included in the text.

The chunk gives the estimated timeline for selection of a Vendor for the City's ERP software and implementation services, and states the City reserves the right to modify or reschedule the timeline as necessary. Dates: Release of Request for Proposals August 16, 2024; Vendor Questions Due August 28, 2024; Vendor Questions Answers Posted September 5, 2024; Proposals Due September 17, 2024; Selection of Finalists October 2024; Software Demos December 2024; Due Diligence Review January 2025; Contract Negotiations January 2025+; Implementation March 2025-January 2027.

An evaluation committee selected by the City will review and score Vendor proposals on five criteria: Software (30 points) for breadth of modules offering all modules required and depth of functionality meeting functional and technical requirements; Technology (15 points) for adherence to IT strategy (platform, database, accessibility) and integration experience and tools offered; Vendor (15 points) for vendor viability and vision, organizational strength and government entity experience; Cost Value (15 points) for software license, subscription and maintenance, implementation services, and terms and conditions; Implementation (25 points) for defined and proven implementation methodology, proposed timeline and staffing, and Go Live for all modules in scope by January 1, 2027. The City may request clarification of submitted materials, reserves the right to select a Vendor based solely on the information submitted and to award a contract without further discussion, and also reserves the right to conduct discussions with Vendors. Based on evaluation, the City will select Vendors invited to the software demo process, notified via e-mail by the date indicated in Section 3, with the notification including a Demo Script document used for on-site demos. The City will conduct pre-demo meetings with finalist Vendors to address questions about logistics of the software demo process and script.

A pre-demo meeting is held to address questions about the logistics of the software demo process and script. Vendors must present functional and technical product demos to the City according to a pre-defined script, and all Vendors must follow this script during their demo process. Demo evaluation criteria include adherence to the script and the ability to successfully demonstrate the product's ability to meet the City's functional and technical requirements. The City reserves the right to request additional information, interviews, follow-up demonstrations or other clarification of proposal information to evaluate final Vendors. An evaluation committee will review and evaluate responses in accordance with criteria identified above; clarification of submitted material may be requested during evaluation. The City may award to the successful Vendor based on the initial proposal, or invite them to demo their solution or enter into contract negotiations; no Contract will be awarded until approved by City Council.

Proposals must be prepared simply and economically with concise descriptions of the Vendor's ability to satisfy the City's functional and technical needs, emphasizing completeness and clarity, and must not exceed 100 pages (a Vendor sample contract is excluded from that limit). Ownership of all data, materials and documentation originated and prepared for the City pursuant to this solicitation belongs to the City; pages considered proprietary must be clearly labeled. Proposals are to be emailed to Thuch.Mam@FederalWayWA.gov and are due on the date indicated in Section 3 of this RFP; submittals received after the deadline will not be considered, and the official submission time is as marked by Outlook in City staff's email inbox. Responses must include only: one electronic PDF copy of the entire RFP proposal in the order defined in the table, not exceeding 100 total pages (excluding sample contracts), and one completed copy of the Requirements document in MS Word format. Submission of a proposal constitutes acknowledgment and acceptance of all terms and conditions in the RFP and its exhibits and attachments.

Proposal submission constitutes acknowledgment and acceptance of all terms and conditions in the RFP and all exhibits and attachments. Pre-bidder questions may be submitted to the City via email at thuch.mam@federalwaywa.gov by the due date outlined in Section 3; the City will post all questions and answers to its website by the date indicated in Section 3. No formal prebidders conference will be held. Vendor responses must include the sections outlined in the RFP; responses that deviate from the requested format may be classified as "non-responsive" and disqualified, and marketing literature should not be included in the proposal.

Section 5 vendor instructions list required proposal sections: 1. Cover Letter (executive summary of proposed software and services for the RFP scope of work, limited to two pages); 2. Requirements (complete the separate Requirements Word document per Section 6 instructions, each requirement rated with a comment on how the function is met, submitted as Section 2 and also in MS Word format without modifying the format, each response limited to 100 words); 3. Pricing (complete Pricing Summary from Exhibit A, covering software and implementation services, comprehensive including all taxes and available discounts, valid for 180 days from response date, with software cost for the user counts defined in the RFP and one sheet per deployment option if applicable (SaaS or on-premises), all implementation costs required for go live including software deployment, data conversion, system configuration, report development, testing and training, and license/maintenance cost for Years 1-10); 4. Implementation (implementation methodology overview including sample project plan with phases, tasks and timeline, City resources roles/responsibilities/average time per month, vendor resources roles/responsibilities/average time per month, process improvement strategy, business change management methodology and tools, data conversion methodology, recommended data conversion by module, testing methodology and tools, training methodology and tools, report development); 5. Support (hours, guaranteed response time, resources available, escalation process, baseline vs. premium support, user groups and conferences). Marketing literature should not be included in the proposal.

Section 5 vendor instructions require proposal content on: post go-live tools and services; backup strategy and support; disaster recovery services (backup, redundancy, location) with baseline support vs. premium level; technology overview covering technical architecture options (hosted, on-premises, SaaS), deployment options, data center locations and redundancy, hardware specifications, mobile hardware and operating system options, remote access capabilities, integration tools and methodologies, and software update scheduling/automatic/timeline; security overview covering security model, standards, security administration (SSO, SAML), multi-factor authentication, and security breach customer communication, response and cost. Vendors must provide references on Exhibit B forms with three current and two prior customers for the proposed software, similar in size and scope to the City's project, with preference for Washington State Public Sector clients. Vendors must indicate whether in the past five years a contract was terminated for convenience, non-performance or any other reason, or legal action with a customer was entered into, describing the situations including name and address of contracting party. Vendors must provide sample contract documents which may include Statement of Work, Perpetual Software License or SaaS License Agreement, Maintenance or Support Agreements, and Service Level Agreements, and must document any exceptions to the RFP content.

Section 6 gives instructions for completing the ERP Requirements document, which is provided as a separate Word document and will become Section 2 of the vendor's proposal. The requirements list is not comprehensive but contains the key requirements used to evaluate proposals and incorporated into the signed contract. Each item carries a ranking: R for Required, I for Important, N for Nice to Have, or E for Explore; software missing a significant number of required features and technology preferences may be eliminated from consideration. Vendors must provide a rating and a comment for every item, with a brief explanation of how the item is supported; no hyperlinks, no references to another line item, all items addressed in the box provided, and no changes to format, font, numbering or page breaks; blank responses may cause the proposal to be considered incomplete and rejected. Rating scale: 4 = Standard and available (out of the box or configuration included in the proposal); 3 = 3rd party software integrated with the proposed solution (name the application); 2 = Modification required (indicate estimated cost); 0 = Not available; F = Future release (indicate anticipated release month and year).

The chunk gives a sample response format for the requirements table, with columns "General" and "Rating and Comment", and an example row "R" for an Audit Trail requirement: audit trail with user, date, time stamp throughout all modules, with before/after values noted as Important; the sample answer states the system logs all transactions and stamps them with user, date, time and before/after values, and that a report can be generated to review audit history. Respondents must not modify the formatting of each cell. A comment of "Standard Functionality" or similar is not acceptable, hyperlinks or references to another cell are not allowed, all answers must be placed in their respective box in the table, and each line-item response is limited to 100 words.

Section 7 of the RFP sets out proposal-process terms: questions, interpretations or clarifications (administrative or technical) must be submitted in writing prior to the date indicated in Section 3 – Timeline, and all pertinent questions will be answered in writing and conveyed to all proposers through the City's website; oral statements about the RFP's meaning or intent by any person are unauthorized and invalid. Proposers who discover any ambiguity, conflict, discrepancy, omission or other error in the RFP or its attachments must immediately notify the City in writing and request modification or clarification; modifications and clarifications are made by addenda posted on the City's website. A proposer who fails to notify the City before the proposal submission date of an error known to them, or that reasonably should have been known, bids at their own risk and, if awarded the contract, is not entitled to additional compensation or time by reason of the error or its later correction. The City may modify the RFP, its key action dates or its attachments prior to the proposal submittal date; addenda are numbered consecutively as a suffix to the RFP reference number, proposers are responsible for incorporating all addenda, and failure to acknowledge and incorporate addenda does not relieve the proposer of meeting all terms and conditions of the RFP and subsequent addenda.

- Addenda will be posted to the City's website.
- Electronic proposals must be accepted on or before the date and time indicated in Section 3 – Timeline, per Section 5 - Vendor Instructions.
- Proposal development costs are entirely the proposer's responsibility and not chargeable to the City; if the City rejects all proposals it is not liable for proposer costs, damages, or loss of anticipated profit.
- Proposals must be delivered by the date in the project schedule; LATE PROPOSALS WILL NOT BE ACCEPTED.
- Proposals become the property of the City and their information becomes public project subject to disclosure laws; the City reserves the right to use any information or ideas contained in the proposal.
- Proposers must notify the City in advance of any proprietary or confidential material and justify non-disclosure; no Vendor may mark its entire submittal proprietary, and the City makes the sole determination of what may be considered proprietary under its interpretation of the Public Disclosure laws.

The City (issuing body) makes the sole determination of what information may be considered proprietary based on its interpretation of Public Disclosure laws; a Vendor cannot mark their entire submittal proprietary. The City may reject any or all proposals and waive any immaterial deviation, and proposals referring to terms and conditions other than the City's may be rejected as non-responsive. The City retains the right to cancel the RFP at any time, including if the project is canceled, the City loses required funding, or it is deemed in the City's best interest; no obligation exists to make an award or pay proposal preparation costs. Insurance requirements: certification of insurance prior to commencement of any work, an underwriter's endorsement with additional insured verbiage, and the surety must be an admitted surety in the State of Washington. Award, if any, will be to the proposer whose proposal best complies with all RFP requirements and any addenda, with evaluation methodology and basis for award described in Section 4 - RFP Evaluation of this RFP.

Exhibit A – Pricing is a template to be used as Section 3 of the response for all "Required" modules; supporting documents may be included and a separate pricing sheet must be provided for each deployment option. The client is the City of Federal Way, WA, with Financials sized at 130 named users and 85 concurrent users, and Human Capital Management sized at 400 FTEs and 744 W2s. Required Financial Modules listed: General Ledger, Budget, Project and Grant Accounting, Purchasing and Contract Management, Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, Project and Grant Accounting (listed twice), Capital Assets, Enterprise Cashiering. Required Human Capital Management Modules: Human Resources, Time and Attendance, Payroll. Pricing structure: Software – Year 1 (with assumptions), Implementation Services (Implementation, Data Conversion, Training, Report Development, Integration, Travel, Other), and Subscription/Maintenance – Years 2-10 priced per year for Year 2 through Year 10, with Sub-Totals for Software, Implementation and Maintenance/License, and a Total.

For each customer the proposer must supply: Name, Employee Count, Population, Contact Name, Contact Telephone and Email, Project Scope, Implementation Duration, Go Live Date, and System Replaced.
